newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends firmer despite U.S. dollar rise.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends firmer despite U.S. dollar rise.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar ended firmer against its U.S. counterpart on Thursday despite the greenback's steady rise against the yen, dealers said.
The local dollar finished at T$27.443, off an intra-day high of T$27.410 but still above Wednesday's T$27.450 close.
Turnover through dealers was a hectic US$400.5 million.

The local currency was relatively stable despite the U.S. dollar's recent appreciation against the Japanese yen as local exporters continued to sell U.S. dollars for their fund needs ahead of the Chinese new year on February 7, dealers said.
Local liquidity demand generally soars ahead of the biggest holiday on the Chinese calendar, which is when firms with good performance reward employees with year-end bonuses.
The dollar on Wednesday vaulted to its highest level against the Japanese yen in just under four years amid a growing sense that Japan would tolerate with weakness in its currency.
Dealers noted that Taiwan's central bank also might sell U.S. dollars to help maintain a stable exchange rate.
"It's obvious the central bank welcomes U.S. dollar selling by local exporters. We suspect the bank may also be taking part in the selling," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
A range of T$27.40-45 range was seen for Friday.
